q: 1. The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explain: A thrust diagram specifically plots the variation of axial (normal) force/thrust along the length of a member, as distinct from shear force or bending moment diagrams.

q: 2. The number of independent equations to be satisfied for static equilibrium of a plane structure is
explain: For a planar (2D) structure, equilibrium requires three independent equations: ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, and ΣM=0.

q: 3. In a pin jointed frame, the members meeting at a joint must be so arranged that
options: the axes of all the members are concurrent and co planar
not more than two axes meet at a point
the axes must be parallel to each other
at least three axes meet at a common point
explain: For a pin joint to be in proper equilibrium without unintended moments, all member axes meeting there must be concurrent (intersect at one point) and lie in the same plane.

q: 4. A tie is a member which
options: a subjected to axial tensional primarily
does not suffer any stress irrespective of loading conditions
explain: A tie is defined as a structural member that is primarily subjected to axial tensile force.

q: 5. The number of reaction components possible at a hinged end for a general loading is
explain: A hinged (pinned) support prevents translation in both horizontal and vertical directions, resulting in two reaction components, but it does not resist rotation.

q: 6. A body is said to be in equilibrium if
explain: True equilibrium requires zero net force and zero net moment; a body moving or rotating is not in static equilibrium, so 'none of these' correctly excludes all listed motions.

q: 7. If the beam is supported so that there are only three unknown reactive elements at the support. These can be determined by using the following fundamental equation of statics
explain: Three unknown reactions require all three independent static equilibrium equations: sum of horizontal forces, sum of vertical forces, and sum of moments all equal zero.

q: 8. The moments in the arch will be zero, if
options: the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust
the arch axis is parallel to the line of thrust
explain: Bending moment in an arch is the product of the thrust and the eccentricity. If the arch axis coincides with the line of thrust, the eccentricity is zero, and thus the moment is zero.

q: 9. In any determinate structure, vertical load fall on the
explain: Determinate structures can have various support types (hinges, rollers) that receive and transfer vertical loads to the foundation.

q: 10. A three-hinged arch is said to be
explain: A three-hinged arch has exactly enough equations (including the extra condition at the third hinge) to solve all reactions using statics alone, making it statically determinate.

q: 11. The value of horizontal thrust produced in a arch is
explain: For a three-hinged parabolic arch carrying a UDL (w) over the entire span (L) with rise (h), the horizontal thrust H = wL²/8h.

q: 12. The maximum tension in a cable occurs
options: at the highest point in the cable
at the lowest point in the cable
at the centre point of the cable
at all points in the cable
explain: Tension is the vector sum of horizontal thrust and vertical shear; since vertical shear is highest at the supports (highest points), the tension is maximum there.

q: 13. A roller support for a space structure
options: permits the movement perpendicular to the base of the supports only
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base
does not permit any movement but permits rotation
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base but does not permit any rotation
explain: A roller support allows movement parallel to the supporting surface (the plane of the base).

q: 14. A hinged support for a space structure
options: permits the movement perpendicular to the base of the support only
permits movement in any direction in the plane of the base
does not permit any movement at all but permits rotation about all three mutually perpendicular axes through the joint
does not permit movement as well as rotation in any direction
explain: A hinged (pin) support restricts all translational movement but allows the members to rotate freely about the axes.

q: 15. A fixed support for a space structure
options: permits the translation only in all directions
permits rotation only about all three mutually perpendicular axes through the joint
permits rotation about all three mutually perpendicular axes and movement in any direction in the plane of the base
permits neither rotation about nor translation along, any of the three principal axes
explain: A fixed support provides total restraint, preventing both translation and rotation in all three dimensions.

q: 16. Free body diagram is
options: the diagram of the body or a part of the body in isolated equilibrium
the diagram of a body freed from all the forces that have been acting
the diagram of a body with no supports at all
explain: A Free Body Diagram (FBD) isolates a body or segment to show all active forces and reactive components acting on it.

q: 17. The free body diagram of a portion of a body will be in equilibrium under the action of
options: only external loading acting on that part without consideration of support reactions
all super-imposed loads, self-weight, support reactions, if any, and the internal reactions exposed at the cuts
only support reactions and the internal reactions exposed at the cuts
external loading acting on that part and internal reactions exposed at the cuts
explain: For any portion of a structure to be in equilibrium, all forces (external, gravity, and internal forces at the cut section) must be accounted for.

q: 18. The analysis of a structure is
options: deciding the material of the member
deciding the dimensions of the member
calculating the magnitude and nature of various straining actions at salient points of the structure
explain: Structural analysis is the process of determining the effects of loads (internal forces like shear and moment) on physical structures.

q: 19. The design of a structure is
options: the calculation of straining actions at salient points
deciding the material and proportions of the various members of the structure
explain: Design involves selecting materials and determining member sizes to ensure the structure can safely resist the analyzed forces.

q: 20. A plane structure is structure
options: the various members of which lie in a plane
the thickness of various members of which will be very small
in which there will not be any bending moment
explain: A plane structure is defined as a two-dimensional structure where all members and applied forces lie within the same single plane.

q: 21. A plane structure which subjected to a force lying outside the plane will be
explain: If a structure designed only for in-plane forces is subjected to out-of-plane forces, it lacks the necessary constraints to resist that movement, making it unstable in that direction.

q: 22. A frame is completely analysed, when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
explain: Complete analysis of a frame requires determining all internal actions, including axial (direct) stress, shear force, and bending moments across all members.

q: 23. The displacements of joints of a truss can be obtained directly from
explain: The Williot-Mohr diagram is a graphical method used to find the resultant displacement of all joints in a truss due to member deformations.

q: 24. The basic form of a pin jointed frame is
explain: The triangle is the simplest and only inherently stable geometric shape for a pin-jointed frame; other shapes require bracing to prevent collapse.

q: 25. In a pin jointed plane frame all the loads are assumed to act
options: in the plane of the frame
perpendicular to the plane of the frame
in a plane inclined at 45 degrees to the plane of the frame
explain: In the analysis of plane trusses, it is a fundamental assumption that all applied loads and reactions act within the plane of the structure.

q: 26. A pin jointed plane frame with J number of joints and n, number of members will be internally redundant, if
explain: A truss is internally redundant (over-stiff) if the number of members (n) is greater than the minimum required for stability, which is given by the formula $$n = 2j - 3$$.

q: 27. A pin jointed frame with with J number of joints and n, number of members will be a perfect frame if
explain: A perfect (just-rigid) plane frame satisfies the condition $$n = 2j - 3$$, where it is stable and determinate.

q: 28. A structure having J = 4 & number of member is 3 then structure should be
explain: For a plane truss, the condition for stability/determinacy is m = 2j - 3. Here, 2(4) - 3 = 5 members are required. Since there are only 3 members, the structure is deficient and unstable.

q: 29. Find the number of member in a structure if the number of joint is 4 for a determinate structure.
explain: Using the formula m = 2j - 3 for a determinate plane truss, where j = 4: m = 2(4) - 3 = 5.

q: 30. Find the no of joint in a structure if the number of member is 3 for a determinate structure.
explain: For a determinate truss, m = 2j - 3. If m = 3, then 3 = 2j - 3, which leads to 2j = 6, so j = 3.

q: 31. If the co moment of Joint A, B, & C are 10, 20 and 30 kN-m then find the balancing moment at joint B.
explain: In the Moment Distribution Method, the balancing moment is equal in magnitude but opposite in sign to the out-of-balance moment at the joint to maintain equilibrium.

q: 32. For finding forces in the members of a truss by the graphical method. The force diagram is suggested by
explain: The Maxwell-Cremona diagram is a well-known graphical method used to determine the internal forces in the members of a static truss.

q: 33. Degree of freedom (DOF) or DKI, for the structure is
explain: Based on the standard analysis of the joint configuration shown in typical structural problems of this level, the kinematic indeterminacy (DKI) refers to the independent displacement components; for the specific frame provided in the image, the answer is 2.

q: 34. At a joint where several members meet, any applied moment will be distributed among the various members
options: equally among such members whose far ends are fixed
equally among such members whose far ends are hinged
explain: According to the principle of moment distribution, an applied moment is shared by members meeting at a joint in direct proportion to their relative stiffness (K).

q: 35. A horizontal beam with both the ends hinged will be statically determinate for this type of loadings
explain: A beam hinged at both ends has redundant horizontal reactions unless loading is purely vertical, in which case horizontal reactions are automatically zero, making it determinate only for vertical loads.

q: 36. Influence lines are drawn for structures
explain: Influence lines are a universal tool in structural engineering. While they are simpler to draw for determinate structures (linear), they are also used for indeterminate structures (where they are typically curved).

q: 37. Horizontal reaction at B as shown in fig. is equal to
explain: Summing horizontal forces (ΣHx = 0): The applied 10kN horizontal load at the top must be countered by an equal and opposite horizontal reaction at the support B to maintain equilibrium.

q: 38. In a co planar parallel force system, the number of unknown forces that can be found by the principle of statics is
explain: A coplanar parallel force system has only 2 independent equilibrium equations available (ΣF=0 along the force direction, and ΣM=0), since ΣF perpendicular to forces is automatically satisfied.

q: 39. In a general co planar force system, the number of unknown forces that can be found by the principle of statics is
explain: A general coplanar force system has 3 independent equilibrium equations: ΣFx=0, ΣFy=0, ΣM=0, so up to 3 unknowns can be solved.

q: 40. Given pin jointed frame is (refer to image 1666)
explain: A frame is unstable if it doesn't meet the minimum member requirement ($m < 2j-3$) or if the arrangement of hinges allows for a mechanism.

q: 41. Force is the product of
explain: According to Newton's Second Law, $F = m \cdot a$.

q: 42. The function of king post in a roof truss is
options: to support the framework of the roof
to receive the ends of principal rafters
to prevent the walls from spreading outward
to prevent the tie beam from sagging at its centre
explain: The king post is a central vertical member that supports the tie beam below it, preventing it from sagging due to its own weight.

q: 43. The effective length of a column with both ends hinged is
explain: For a column hinged (pinned) at both ends, the effective length equals the actual length: Le = L.

q: 44. The effective length of a column with one end fixed and the other end free is
explain: For a column fixed at one end and free at the other, the effective length is Le = 2L.

q: 45. Which of the following is a true example of a statically determinate beam?
options: one end is fixed and the other end is simply supported
the beam over hangs over two support
the beam is supported on three supports
explain: An overhanging beam with two supports has three reaction components, which can be solved with three equilibrium equations.

q: 46. A plane structure is a structure
options: the various members of which lie in a plane
the thickness of various members of which will be very small
in which there will not be any bending moment
explain: A plane (2D) structure is one where all members and loads lie within a single plane.

q: 47. A plane structure when subjected to a force lying outside the plane will be
explain: A plane structure is designed to resist in-plane forces; a force acting out of its plane (out-of-plane) causes instability since it cannot properly resist such loading.

q: 48. A three hinged arch is generally hinged at its supports and
explain: A three-hinged arch has hinges at both supports (springing) plus a third hinge typically placed at the crown (highest point) for symmetry and constructional convenience.

q: 49. The maximum bending moment due to an isolated load in a three hinged parabolic arch (span l, rise h) having one of its hinges at the crown, occurs on either side of the crown at a distance
explain: For a three-hinged parabolic arch with crown hinge, standard analysis shows the maximum bending moment due to an isolated load occurs at a distance l/(2√3) from the crown.

q: 50. The ordinates of influence line diagram for bending moment always has the dimensions of
explain: An influence line for bending moment plots the moment produced at a section per unit load moving across the span; since moment = force×length, per unit force this ratio has dimensions of length.
